title: WebSocket Event Catalog
purpose: Catalog all Socket.IO events by direction (server→client, client→server), identify dead/missing events, and map handling components
audience: Full-stack developers, QA engineers, platform maintainers
description: A comprehensive catalog of Socket.IO events in the PoDM system. Server-to-client events include new_message, message_deleted, and conversation_read — all actively emitted by the server. Client-to-server events include join_conversation and leave_conversation for room management. A dead event (message_updated) has frontend listeners registered but is never emitted by the server. Two gaps exist: no typing indicators (typing/stop_typing) and no offline delivery mechanism — messages are loaded via REST on next page load.

preconditions: Socket.IO server initialized with CORS origins configured (podm.app, *.pages.dev, localhost:5173)
JWT auth middleware attached to Socket.IO server for connection validation
Frontend components have Socket.IO client initialized and connected
postconditions: All active events are properly handled on both server and client sides
Dead events identified for cleanup or implementation
Missing events documented for future implementation (typing indicators, offline delivery)

nodes.label: socket.ts — Connection Handler
nodes.description: Socket.IO server init with CORS, JWT auth middleware via supabase.auth.getUser(), room management (join/leave via socket.join/socket.leave)

nodes.label: new_message
nodes.description: Server→Client. Emitted to conversation-{id} room via io.to(room).emit() after message DB insert succeeds. Payload: full message object with sender, text, content, timestamp.

nodes.label: message_deleted
nodes.description: Server→Client. Emitted to conversation-{id} room after soft-delete (UPDATE SET is_deleted=true). Payload: { messageId }.

nodes.label: conversation_read
nodes.description: Server→Client. Emitted only to the sender's own socket (not broadcast to room) when conversation marked as read. Payload: { conversation_id }.

nodes.label: join_conversation
nodes.description: Client→Server. Client emits with conversationId. Server calls socket.join(conversation-{id}). Requires valid JWT and conversation participation.

nodes.label: leave_conversation
nodes.description: Client→Server. Client emits with conversationId. Server calls socket.leave(conversation-{id}).

nodes.label: message_updated [DEAD]
nodes.description: DEAD EVENT. Registered as listener in FanMessages.tsx and CreatorMessages.tsx but never emitted by server. No message edit functionality implemented.

nodes.label: FanMessages.tsx Listeners
nodes.description: Frontend component registers Socket.IO event listeners: new_message (append to conversation), message_deleted (remove from UI), conversation_read (update read status), message_updated (dead — never fires)

nodes.label: CreatorMessages.tsx Listeners
nodes.description: Frontend component registers Socket.IO event listeners: new_message (append to conversation), message_deleted (remove from UI), conversation_read (update read status), message_updated (dead — never fires)

nodes.label: typing [MISSING]
nodes.description: MISSING EVENT. No typing/stop_typing events implemented. Users cannot see when the other participant is typing.

nodes.label: Offline Delivery Gap
nodes.description: MISSING FEATURE. No offline message queuing. If recipient's Socket.IO disconnected, messages are not delivered. Recipient must REST GET /api/v1/messages/conversations/:id on next page load to see missed messages.

nodes.label: message.service.ts — Event Emission
nodes.description: Message service triggers Socket.IO emission after DB operations: sendDirectMessage → emit new_message; deleteMessage → emit message_deleted; markConversationRead → emit conversation_read

validationRules: join_conversation requires valid JWT and conversation participant check
Event payloads must include required fields per event type
conversation_read emitted only to reader's own socket, not broadcast
businessRules: new_message event is the primary real-time delivery mechanism
message_deleted triggers UI removal in conversation view
conversation_read updates unread badge count for the reader only
No typing indicators — conversations lack real-time typing awareness
No offline message queue — REST API is the fallback delivery mechanism
securityConsiderations: Socket.IO connections authenticated via JWT on handshake
Room membership gated by conversation participation — users can only join rooms they belong to
Event payloads contain full message data including text content
No E2EE — events transmitted in plaintext over WebSocket (mitigated by WSS)
Dead event handlers consume memory unnecessarily
performanceConsiderations: Each new_message event broadcast to all room participants — O(n) per message
No event batching — each operation generates individual events
Frontend listeners run on main thread — many concurrent events could cause jank
Dead event listeners consume minimal memory but accumulate technical debt

annotations.label: 🔴 Dead Event: message_updated
annotations.description: Registered in FanMessages.tsx and CreatorMessages.tsx but server never emits it. Indicates planned message edit feature not implemented.

annotations.label: 🟡 Missing: Typing Indicators
annotations.description: No typing/stop_typing events. Users cannot see real-time typing status in conversations.

annotations.label: 🟡 Missing: Offline Delivery
annotations.description: No offline message queue. Disconnected recipients must REST fetch missed messages. No push notification fallback.

annotations.label: 💚 Active: new_message — Server emits after DB insert

annotations.label: 💚 Active: conversation_read — Server emits to reader
